correctness.rationale: The graph bipartition separates original-vertex and subdivision-vertex footprints; any completed history bijects with an ordered (n-1)-vertex cover, an ordered legal edge-cover of K_n, and an interleaving. Last-edge classification proves \(a_{r,k}=r(r-1)a_{r-1,k-1}+\binom r2 a_{r-2,k-1}\); all feasible lengths are constructible, and factorial extreme counts follow. Independent exhaustive dynamic programming on original graph neighborhoods for n=2,3,4,5 agrees with every polynomial coefficient. Finite checks are not the general proof.

value.rationale: The exact polynomial counts every legal full domination history of a natural dense-graph incidence family, refining known scalar endpoints and distinguishing ordered histories from ordinary unordered edge covers. A short recurrence permits all coefficient counts, while closed shortest/longest history multiplicities and gapless support quantify the combinatorial range of greedy covering behavior for arbitrarily large n.
